strengths: Clear problem motivation with compelling frequency-domain example (Section 3.2) demonstrating time-domain saliency limitations for time series
Sound mathematical framework: Complex IG derivation (Lemma 4.2, Definition 4.1) rigorously extends IG to complex inputs while preserving completeness and path independence axioms
Breadth of applicability: Unified framework supporting six transform families (DFT, STFT, DWT, ICA, STL, Complex Cepstrum) substantially exceeds prior work

Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation: Combines axiomatic guarantees, mechanistic analysis, insertion/deletion tests, quantitative CPD benchmarks, and three real-world case studies with interpretable insights
Real-world demonstrations yield actionable insights (identifying spurious vs. legitimate model signals; isolating disease vs. artifact components; diagnosing model deficiencies)
Open-source implementation with detailed algorithms enhances reproducibility and adoption potential
Well-presented with effective visualizations that clearly illustrate concepts and model behavior
weaknesses: Domain choice is critical but unaddressed: Paper acknowledges poor domain selection yields 'semantically misleading' saliency maps yet provides no guidance on selection, validation, or detection of poor choices. Practical utility for non-expert practitioners is unclear.

Evaluation methodology gap: Qualitative case studies intentionally choose domains with ground-truth knowledge of interpretability; quantitative benchmarks use fixed domains. This gap makes it unclear whether improvements depend on informed domain selection or the method itself.

Limited sample sizes undermine real-world claims: Heart rate evaluation on one subject's 2-hour session; EEG analysis on single recording; forecasting on synthetic data only. Held-out test set evaluation across multiple subjects/conditions is needed.

Baseline selection underexplored: Method relies on zero baseline with minimal investigation of sensitivity to baseline choice, particularly problematic for transformed domains where meaningful baselines may differ from zero (e.g., mean spectrum for frequency domain).

Computational overhead not analyzed: Acknowledged overhead from inverse transforms (Remark 4.6) but no timing comparisons, scaling analysis, or computational cost vs. transform type. Critical for practical adoption, especially for transforms requiring matrix inversion (ICA).

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Main paper compares only TIMEX++ and TIMING; VIL relegated to appendix equivalence proof; FreqRISE comparison shows mixed results (CDIG sometimes loses). Comprehensive baseline comparisons belong in main paper.

Mechanistic analysis limited to toy model: Section 4.2 analyzes single-channel CNN with sinusoidal signals; unclear if insights transfer to realistic deep networks. More complex architecture analysis needed.

Transform invertibility assumptions not examined: ICA has practical issues (non-identifiability, numerical stability); paper doesn't discuss when assumptions are reasonable or propose handling mechanisms for edge cases.
Statistical rigor gaps: Benchmark tables lack significance tests; CPD metric improvements sometimes fall within standard error bounds; unclear which differences are statistically meaningful.

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear limitations of time-domain saliency for time series; elegant mechanistic demonstration in Section 3.2

Technically sound theoretical contribution: extension of Integrated Gradients to complex-valued domains using Wirtinger calculus, with maintained axiomatic properties (path independence, completeness)
General, transform-agnostic framework supporting six diverse transforms (DFT, STFT, DWT, ICA, STL, Cepstrum) compared to single-domain focus of prior methods

Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation: mechanistic analysis, qualitative case studies across three real-world applications with different model architectures, quantitative insertion/deletion faithfulness tests, and comparisons with multiple baselines

Practical utility convincingly demonstrated: case studies show domain-appropriate saliency maps reveal interpretable insights (e.g., spurious artifacts in PPG, isolated epileptic sources) that time-domain IG cannot capture
Honest and thorough limitations discussion including acknowledgment of risks from poor transform selection and gap between qualitative and quantitative evaluation
Reproducibility commitment via promised open-source TensorFlow/PyTorch library
Clear presentation with good motivation and logical flow
weaknesses: Limited novelty: computing IG in transformed space builds on prior work (MIX for Haar-DWT); extension to multiple domains is incremental despite breadth being valuable

Fundamental evaluation methodology gap: qualitative evaluation intentionally leverages domain knowledge to select appropriate transforms (defeating objectivity), while quantitative evaluation uses standardized fixed transforms (mismatched to paper's premise). No principled guidance for practitioners to select domains blindly in novel applications

Mixed and modest quantitative results: Table 2 shows CDIG inconsistently outperforming TIMING (e.g., 0.463 vs 0.207 on PAM); claim that different domains excel on different datasets is post-hoc observation without principled selection method. Standard errors sometimes exceed method differences
Incomplete comparisons: FreqRISE comparison limited to AudioMNIST; MIX only compared on Haar-DWT; no runtime/computational cost analysis despite acknowledged overhead
Restrictive assumptions: invertibility and differentiability requirements exclude important transforms; no treatment of approximately invertible or ill-conditioned transforms

Limited experimental scope: only three real-world case studies (potentially cherry-picked for favorable outcomes); no demonstrated failure cases or examples where time-domain IG was preferable; foundation model example uses synthetic data with ground-truth trend/seasonality
Underexplored baseline and path sensitivity: focus on zero-signal baseline only; complex-valued domain sensitivity not discussed; linear integration paths only despite other options existing

Reproducibility concerns: code unavailable for review despite central role in contributions; unclear insertion/deletion protocol details; ICA hyperparameters buried in appendix without sensitivity analysis

Insufficient technical validation of complex-valued extension: proofs in Appendix B lack sufficient detail; no analysis of numerical stability when T^{-1} is ill-conditioned; autograd conjugate gradient interaction with complex IG not thoroughly discussed

Medical applications (seizure detection, heart rate) require more rigorous validation for high-stakes settings; impact statement acknowledges risks but provides limited mitigation beyond 'domain expertise'
